newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philrealty scales down 1997 net projection.
newsitem.headline: Philrealty scales down 1997 net projection.

text.p: Philippine Realty Holdings Corp (Philrealty) said on Monday it had scaled down its 1997 net income projection due to the slowdown in demand for high-end residential apartments.
The revised forecast was set at between 800 million and 900 million pesos, against an earlier target of just over one billion pesos.
Last year, Philrealty posted a net income of 1.036 billion peso, about 800 million pesos of which were extraordinary gains from the sale of its holdings in Philippine Racing Club Inc.
For the first half of the year, the company was expecting a net income of 175 million pesos, up from 105.75 million pesos in the year-earlier period.
"Due to some delays, we have scaled down our projection," Philrealty executive vice president Amador Bacani told reporters.
Bacani noted that the bulk of the revenues will start coming in the second half of the year with the launching and pre-selling of four new projects.
Bacani said the slowdown in demand for high-end residential apartments had prompted the company to redesign and delay one of its projects in the prime Ortigas business district.
"Due to the weak demand, we are increasing the amount of saleable space and making the price more competitive," Bacani said.
The company has also redesigned other residential projects to cater for middle-class buyers, Bacani said.

Among those projects which would be launched later this year included the second tower of a residential complex in suburban Quezon city, a residential condominium in downtown Malate district, a high-end residential project in Bonifacio city, and a leisure estate and country club east of Manila.
